engineering-preview-terminated-on-every-exitengineering-verification-tooling-robustness0.625 of 0.625 (major)passI side with judges A and B. In all four copies (repository and bootstrap verify and inspect), startPreview spawns `process.execPath` running vite&#39;s own `bin/vite.js preview` directly. The child process is therefore the preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. In verify&#39;s renderEveryStep, startPreview, chromium.launch(), and every later step check all sit inside one try, and its finally runs `await browser?.close()` and then `await preview?.stop()`. Success, a failing outline or render check, a browser launch failure, and any later thrown error all pass through that cleanup. In inspect&#39;s main, every step after the preview starts (chromium.launch, the capture passes, setting exitCode) is inside a try whose finally awaits preview.stop(). stop() sends SIGTERM, schedules SIGKILL after 3s, and awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; promise, so it both terminates the server and waits for it to exit. The bootstrap template copies have the same code. Judge C points to the readiness-timeout branch, which sends SIGKILL and throws without awaiting exit. That branch runs inside startPreview before the preview has started (startPreview has not returned), so it is not one of the exit paths the requirement and guidance name. It also still terminates the server process itself with SIGKILL, which cannot be ignored. In main(), checkSampleRegistration runs after the build and before any browser work. An unregistered slug, a missing registry, a wrong title or a missing loader/source each throws PhaseError(&#39;sample&#39;). The catch handler prints `FAIL verify [sample]: ...` and calls process.exit(1). If steps are present but absent or out of order, against the nine normative titles and captions in verify.config.json, the verifier fails at explicit outline checks. A wrong step count fails with &#39;sample has N steps, expected 9&#39;. A title or caption mismatch at any step fails with `step i: title is ...`. Both use the [outline] phase, so they report that the sample does not match the outline. Focused E2E faults cover these cases. &#39;a registry without the sample&#39; expects a non-zero exit, `FAIL verify [sample]`, /not registered/ and no [render] output. Other faults cover a wrong title, swapped steps 3/4 and the 8-step case. Judges A and C are borne out. Judge B&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. It is true that a route with no steps at all hits a waitForSelector timeout, which reports in the [render] phase. But that is not an unrelated browser timeout. It is a purpose-built check: `step 0: &lt;route&gt; did not render a presentation`, which names the phase, the step and the route. The waitForSelector timeout is caught, and a purpose-built PhaseError(&#39;render&#39;) says the route did not render a presentation. That output names the phase. Focused end-to-end tests check each case for a non-zero exit, the `FAIL verify [phase]` text, and a matching message. It is a purpose-built check: `step 0: &lt;route&gt; did not render a presentation`, which names the phase, the step and the route. In all four copies (repository and bootstrap verify and inspect), startPreview spawns `process.execPath` running vite&#39;s own `bin/vite.js preview` directly. The child process is therefore the preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. In verify&#39;s renderEveryStep, startPreview, chromium.launch(), and every later step check all sit inside one try, and its finally runs `await browser?.close()` and then `await preview?.stop()`. Success, a failing outline or render check, a browser launch failure, and any later thrown error all pass through that cleanup. In inspect&#39;s main, every step after the preview starts (chromium.launch, the capture passes, setting exitCode) is inside a try whose finally awaits preview.stop(). stop() sends SIGTERM, schedules SIGKILL after 3s, and awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; promise, so it both terminates the server and waits for it to exit. The bootstrap template copies have the same code. Judge C points to the readiness-timeout branch, which sends SIGKILL and throws without awaiting exit. That branch runs inside startPreview before the preview has started (startPreview has not returned), so it is not one of the exit paths the requirement and guidance name. It also still terminates the server process itself with SIGKILL, which cannot be ignored. In all four copies (repository and bootstrap verify and inspect), startPreview spawns `process.execPath` running vite&#39;s own `bin/vite.js preview` directly. The child process is therefore the preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. In verify&#39;s renderEveryStep, startPreview, chromium.launch(), and every later step check all sit inside one try, and its finally runs `await browser?.close()` and then `await preview?.stop()`. Success, a failing outline or render check, a browser launch failure, and any later thrown error all pass through that cleanup. In inspect&#39;s main, every step after the preview starts (chromium.launch, the capture passes, setting exitCode) is inside a try whose finally awaits preview.stop(). stop() sends SIGTERM, schedules SIGKILL after 3s, and awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; promise, so it both terminates the server and waits for it to exit. The bootstrap template copies have the same code. Judge C points to the readiness-timeout branch, which sends SIGKILL and throws without awaiting exit. That branch runs inside startPreview before the preview has started (startPreview has not returned), so it is not one of the exit paths the requirement and guidance name. It also still terminates the server process itself with SIGKILL, which cannot be ignored. The criterion requires cleanup on the named paths after the preview has started, and those paths do await exit. tests/e2e/verify.test.ts also asserts that no `vite.js preview` process remains after success, after every fault, and after a preview start failure.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs:24-27 spawn(process.execPath, [vite, &#39;preview&#39;, ...]): the child is the vite server itself, with no npm/npx wrapper","scripts/lib/preview.mjs:50-56 stop(): child.kill(&#39;SIGTERM&#39;), a SIGKILL timer after 3000ms, then `await exited`","scripts/verify.mjs:43-86 the try covers startPreview, chromium.launch().catch(throw PhaseError), and all step checks; the finally awaits browser.close() and preview.stop()","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:97-118 the preview starts, then try { chromium.launch ... capture passes } finally { browser close; await preview.stop() }","The bootstrap copies skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs:21-59, verify.mjs:39-87 and inspect-presentation.mjs:92-119 have the same cleanup","tests/e2e/verify.test.ts:41,176,189 assert that processExists(vite.js preview) is false after the passing run, after each fault, and after a preview start failure"],"citations":[{"path":"scripts/lib/preview.mjs","start_line":20,"end_line":59},{"path":"scripts/verify.mjs","start_line":39,"end_line":87},{"path":"scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","start_line":92,"end_line":124},{"path":"skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs","start_line":20,"end_line":59},{"path":"skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","start_line":39,"end_line":87},{"path":"skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","start_line":92,"end_line":124},{"path":"tests/e2e/verify.test.ts","start_line":167,"end_line":193}],"search_scope":[],"missing_obligation":""},{"id":"engineering-tests-wait-on-state","verdict":"pass","rationale":"I rule judges A and B&#39;s pass. That makes the browser tests tests/integration/inspect.test.ts, tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts and tests/e2e/verify.test.ts. All three are quoted in full or in the parts that touch a browser. No transition is involved, so there is no state to wait for. Judge C&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. The test does not sleep: it awaits the script&#39;s exit and then asserts on the screenshots it produced. The only test-side fixed delays are in tests/unit/no-replay.test.tsx:19 and tests/unit/stage.test.tsx:180. The child process is the preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. In verify&#39;s renderEveryStep, startPreview, chromium.launch() and every later step check sit in one try block. Its finally block awaits browser?.close() and then preview?.stop(). That covers success, a failing outline or render check, a browser launch failure and any later thrown error. In inspect&#39;s main, startPreview returns before the try block. After that, the browser launch, the capture passes and setting exitCode all run inside a try block whose finally block awaits preview.stop(). Because the finally block runs before the rejection reaches main().catch, the server is stopped before process.exit(1). stop() sends SIGTERM, schedules a SIGKILL fallback after 3 seconds, and awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; promise, so it terminates the server and waits for it to exit. The readiness-timeout branch, which sends SIGKILL without awaiting exit, runs inside startPreview before the preview has started. It is not one of the exit paths after start that the guidance lists. The bootstrap template copies are identical. The e2e tests also assert that no &#39;vite.js preview&#39; process remains after success, after each fault, and after a preview start failure.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs:24 spawns process.execPath with [vite, &#39;preview&#39;, ...], where vite is node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js. In all four copies (repository and bootstrap verify and inspect), startPreview spawns `process.execPath` running vite&#39;s own `bin/vite.js preview` directly. The child process is therefore the preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. In verify&#39;s renderEveryStep, startPreview, chromium.launch(), and every later step check all sit inside one try, and its finally runs `await browser?.close()` and then `await preview?.stop()`. Success, a failing outline or render check, a browser launch failure, and any later thrown error all pass through that cleanup. In inspect&#39;s main, every step after the preview starts (chromium.launch, the capture passes, setting exitCode) is inside a try whose finally awaits preview.stop(). stop() sends SIGTERM, schedules SIGKILL after 3s, and awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; promise, so it both terminates the server and waits for it to exit. The bootstrap template copies have the same code. Judge C points to the readiness-timeout branch, which sends SIGKILL and throws without awaiting exit.
